title: Enterprise Gatebook & Runtime Fallbacks for Hosted Chat + Tool Calls
creator: Elena Morales
description: Objective: Define an operational 'gatebook' and automated runtime fallback matrix that governs how enterprise-hosted API feature requests (multi-turn chat, streaming, function/tool calls, structured outputs) are admitted to production, and how the runtime should degrade gracefully when capacity, model quality, or security constraints are hit. Focus on minimizing outage blast radius for high-value tenants while preserving developer experience for self-serve use cases.
background: We receive frequent enterprise requests that push combinations of features (long-duration streaming + tool chains + structured outputs). These requests have varied SLA expectations and risk profiles. Current onboarding is manual and inconsistent; incidents show model fallbacks and cross-tenant capacity contention causing latency and cost spikes. Need a systematic gate + runtime policy matrix so we can automate admission and enforce safe fallbacks.
goals: Create deterministic eligibility checks for enterprise feature admission
Define runtime fallback hierarchy by signal (capacity, latency SLO breach, quality regression, security flag)
Expose clear tenant-facing contract (what will be guaranteed vs best-effort)
Provide operational runbooks and dashboard alerts tied to gates and fallbacks
acceptance_criteria: Gatebook doc published in Confluence and reviewed by Security and Sales Engineering
Runtime can route failing requests to specified fallback model/variant automatically
Operator dashboard shows gate status per tenant and last 30-day fallback events
Canary rollout plan for gate enforcement across 10 pilot tenants with rollback criteria
comments: 2026-02-26 - PM kickoff: collected inbound requests from top 8 enterprise accounts; common themes are long streaming sessions + tool chains. Action: compile sample request traces (Ravi)
2026-03-01 - Eng sync: ENG-2148 will add tenant-aware capacity tagging. Trade-off: tagging increases scheduling complexity but enables strict isolation policies.
2026-03-03 - Security review request filed (SR-337) to evaluate structured output exfiltration risk; preliminary note: use L4 output sanitizers before admission.
2026-03-06 - Solutions Eng feedback: sales will need a templated SLAs and negotiated fallback contract; recommend 'gold/silver/bronze' tiers in gatebook.

2026-03-08 - Draft gatebook posted to Confluence; seeking PM+Eng+Sec reviews. Noted open question: should grafted fallback happen per-request or per-tenant session? (Engineering prefers per-request for lower blast radius)
2026-03-09 - Design provided mockups for tenant dashboard showing gate status and recent fallbacks; awaiting final UX sign-off.
decisions: Use tenant-tier model (Gold/Silver/Bronze) for admission policies
Fallback hierarchy: same-architecture quantized variant -> cheaper model -> degraded streaming (batching + shorter transcripts) -> graceful reject with clear error payload
Per-request fallback enforcement vs per-session: choose per-request—less privileged exposure and more granular observability
tradeoffs: Per-request fallback increases runtime decision overhead and latency on edge cases vs per-session reduces granularity
Strict admission decreases friction for reliability but increases sales gating work and onboarding time
Using cheaper model variants reduces cost but may cause quality regressions; require preflight eval sets for each tenant
next_steps: Finalize gate eligibility rules and map to tenant tiers (PM/Ravi) - target 2026-03-13
Engineering to prototype per-request fallback manager and submit RFC (ENG-2148) - target 2026-03-18
Legal/Sales to draft fallback SLA text and negotiable parameters - target 2026-03-15
Select 10 pilot tenants and run canary for 2 weeks; collect quality and latency metrics - target start 2026-03-22
risks: Customer churn risk if fallbacks degrade perceived quality and contracts aren't clear
Operational complexity: increased scheduling and per-request policy checks may introduce new failure modes
Potential compliance issues for regulated tenants; must run security review and sign-off before admission
notes_for_engineering: Expose tenant-tier and request-label (streaming/tool-call/structured-output) in the routing decision API
Add hooks to emit structured telemetry events when fallbacks occur (tenant, reason, latency delta, token delta)
Fallback decision must be idempotent and deterministic for retry semantics
notes_for_sales: Provide templated fallback language and examples for Gold/Silver/Bronze tiers
Recommend offering a pilot period with lowered SLA but dedicated engineering onboarding
